entry.title: Orchid replication operations
entry.summary: Operational checkpoint details for Orchid replication

body:
Overview. Orchid is a document-processing experiment used in internal examples. This introduction discusses naming, ownership, and general deployment context without specifying any checkpoint value.

Background. Teams first prepare a workspace, validate permissions, and record a run identifier. Operators also review storage capacity and confirm that monitoring dashboards are available.

Procedure. The replication job starts only after inputs pass validation. Routine health messages are emitted during execution, while unrelated maintenance guidance remains in a separate runbook.

Recovery. If a worker exits, operators inspect its log and retain intermediate artifacts. This paragraph describes recovery behavior but does not define the checkpoint interval.

Authoritative setting. The Orchid replication protocol uses a 37 minute checkpoint interval during the evaluated run. This value applies to the frozen diagnostic configuration.

Closing. Reports should preserve the configuration version and should not generalize one diagnostic setting to every deployment.

Introduction. Cedar clients maintain a local cache to reduce repeated reads. The opening section lists ordinary installation steps and compatibility notes but contains no invalidation rule.

Setup. A client opens the cache directory, checks file permissions, and records its runtime version. These steps are operational prerequisites rather than cache semantics.

Observation. Logging may include request latency, payload size, and server identifiers. Those diagnostics are useful for support but do not decide whether a cached record remains valid.

Versioned rule. Cedar client version 3 invalidates a cached record when its revision token changes. The token comparison occurs before the cached value is returned.

Examples. A changed token causes a refresh, whereas an unchanged token permits reuse. Example identifiers are illustrative and are not additional rules.

Appendix. Administrators may rotate logs and archive old traces. This final section does not alter the versioned invalidation behavior.

entry.title: Atlas SDK resilience configuration
entry.summary: Retry count and timeout behavior for Atlas SDK 2.0

body:
Context. Atlas SDK 2.0 includes several resilience controls. The introduction distinguishes transport failures from application errors and asks readers to retain version conditions.

Retry rule. Atlas SDK 2.0 defaults to five retry attempts for transient transport failures. Applications may override the retry count in their client configuration.

Diagnostics. Each attempt records a request identifier and a compact failure category. These fields support debugging but do not change the retry default.

Deployment. Operators should validate credentials and endpoint reachability before attributing failures to retry behavior. Environment checks are outside the retry policy.

Timeout rule. The evaluated Atlas client uses a 12 second per-attempt timeout. The timeout is measured separately for each retry attempt.

Limitations. The two settings describe the frozen SDK 2.0 diagnostic and are not measurements of user satisfaction or production reliability.

Opening record. Reviewers retained the first signed worksheet before any consolidation step. The worksheet is kept with its original timestamp and author identifier.

Preparation note. Files were sorted into a stable order, blank pages were removed, and page counts were recorded for later inspection.

Middle record. Two independent reviewers approved the retained worksheet. Their decisions were recorded separately before the records were combined.

Processing note. The archive job copied source files, verified byte counts, and produced a local inventory for the diagnostic bundle.

Closing record. A later reviewer withdrew approval after finding an incorrect date. The withdrawal remains visible beside the earlier decisions.

Scope note. This compact example tests document coverage only; it does not estimate real review quality or reviewer behavior.
